title: The Inverse Galois Problem
description: An open problem asking whether every finite group occurs as the Galois group of some Galois extension of ℚ. We formalize the conjecture, prove cyclotomic realizations for abelian groups, and document what remains unknown.

overview.historicalContext:
The Inverse Galois Problem (IGP) emerged naturally from Galois theory, which Évariste Galois developed in 1832 (published posthumously). Galois theory provides a dictionary between field extensions and groups: every Galois extension K/F has a group Gal(K/F), and vice versa. But the 'vice versa' direction—given a group G, finding K—is the challenge.

Hilbert in 1892 proved that all symmetric groups Sₙ are realizable using his irreducibility theorem. Shafarevich's 1954 theorem resolved all solvable groups. The problem remains open in general.

The IGP is intimately connected to understanding the absolute Galois group Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ), one of the most mysterious objects in mathematics. It is related to Grothendieck's 'Esquisse d'un Programme' (1984), which proposed using the IGP to understand the absolute Galois group via its action on algebraic curves.

As of 2026, the general problem remains unsolved, though most finite simple groups have been realized over ℚ. The holdout cases include certain sporadic simple groups.
overview.problemStatement:
**The Inverse Galois Problem**: Does every finite group G occur as the Galois group Gal(K/ℚ) of some Galois extension K of ℚ?

Formally: ∀ (G : finite group), ∃ (K : Galois extension of ℚ), Gal(K/ℚ) ≅ G.

Galois theory gives us a rich supply of examples. The cyclotomic field ℚ(ζₙ) has Galois group (ℤ/nℤ)ˣ. But can we realize EVERY finite group? The answer is unknown.

**Known results**:
- All abelian groups: Kronecker-Weber theorem gives all abelian extensions of ℚ as cyclotomic subfields
- All solvable groups: Shafarevich (1954)
- All symmetric groups Sₙ: Hilbert's irreducibility theorem
- Most finite simple groups: case-by-case constructions
- **Open**: the general case
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization spans three files (1518 lines total). **InverseGalois.lean** (799 lines) states the IGP, proves cyclotomic realizations for abelian groups via Gal(Q(zeta_n)/Q) ≅ (Z/nZ)^x, and axiomatizes Kronecker-Weber and Shafarevich. **AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensions.lean** (534 lines, 0 sorries) proves the sharp solvability threshold: S_n solvable iff n ≤ 4, with 15 sections covering small symmetric groups, alternating group structure, radical solvability, Galois properties, index theorems, and factorial identities. **AbelRuffini.lean** (185 lines) connects to Mathlib's Abel-Ruffini infrastructure. Key proof: Gal(X^3-2/Q) ≅ S_3 proved from scratch using 3|deg (prime irred), deg|6 (Gal embeds S_3), 2|deg (cube root of unity exists), therefore deg=6=|S_3|.
keyInsights: Cyclotomic fields provide a systematic source of abelian Galois groups over ℚ
The Galois group Gal(ℚ(ζₙ)/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/nℤ)ˣ whenever the n-th cyclotomic polynomial is irreducible over ℚ
The n-th cyclotomic polynomial is ALWAYS irreducible over ℚ (Gauss, 1801)
Every finite abelian group is isomorphic to a subgroup of some (ℤ/nℤ)ˣ
Shafarevich's theorem extends this to ALL finite solvable groups
Symmetric groups Sₙ are realizable via Hilbert irreducibility theorem
The general case reduces to the question: does Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) surject onto all finite groups?

sections.title: The Inverse Galois Conjecture
sections.summary: Formal statement of the IGP as a Lean proposition. Marked as an open problem with sorry - no proof is known for the general case.

sections.title: Cyclotomic Fields Are Galois
sections.summary: CyclotomicField n ℚ is Galois over ℚ (IsCyclotomicExtension.isGalois), and its Galois group is abelian (commutative).

sections.title: Galois Group ≅ (ZMod n)ˣ
sections.summary: The Galois group of the n-th cyclotomic polynomial is isomorphic to (ZMod n)ˣ. The irreducibility of cyclotomic polynomials over ℚ (a classical theorem) is axiomatized here.

sections.title: Specific Cyclic Group Realizations
sections.summary: Concrete examples: (ZMod 4)ˣ has order 2 (gives ℤ/2ℤ), (ZMod 5)ˣ has order 4 (gives ℤ/4ℤ), (ZMod p)ˣ has order p-1 for prime p. These groups are cyclic.

sections.title: Abelian Groups: Kronecker-Weber
sections.summary: Every finite abelian group is realizable. This follows from the Kronecker-Weber theorem (every abelian extension of ℚ is contained in a cyclotomic field). Stated as an axiom pending Lean formalization of Kronecker-Weber.

sections.title: Solvable Groups: Shafarevich 1954
sections.summary: Every finite solvable group is realizable (Shafarevich's theorem). This deep result uses class field theory. A5 is proved non-solvable, showing the theorem doesn't cover A5 trivially.

sections.title: Symmetric Groups: Hilbert
sections.summary: Sₙ is realizable for all n (Hilbert's irreducibility theorem). Stated with sorry as the proof requires results not yet in Mathlib.

sections.title: What Remains Open
sections.summary: Documentation of the mathematical landscape: what's known, what's open, connections to absolute Galois groups, the Langlands programme, and Grothendieck's programme.

sections.title: Small Symmetric Groups Are Solvable (Extension File)
sections.summary: In AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensions.lean: S_0, S_1 solvable (subsingleton), S_2 solvable (commutative via decide), S_3 solvable (exact sequence A_3 → S_3 → Z^x), S_4 solvable (exact sequence A_4 → S_4 → Z^x). All fully proved.

sections.title: Sharp Threshold: S_n Solvable iff n ≤ 4
sections.summary: In AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensions.lean: S_n is solvable iff n ≤ 4. Uses Equiv.Perm.not_solvable for n ≥ 5. This is the fundamental threshold in the Abel-Ruffini theorem.

sections.title: Galois Group Properties and Cardinalities
sections.summary: In AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensions.lean: Galois group properties, subgroup solvability preservation, alternating non-solvability for n ≥ 5, factorial identities and cardinalities for Perm (Fin n), index theorems, and chain properties. 57 theorems total, all fully proved.

conclusion.summary: The Inverse Galois Problem remains one of the great open questions in algebra. Across 1518 lines in 3 files (75 theorems, 2 axioms, 2 sorries), we formalize: the IGP conjecture, cyclotomic Galois theory with Gal(Q(zeta_n)/Q) ≅ (Z/nZ)^x, Gal(X^3-2/Q) ≅ S_3 proved from scratch, the sharp solvability threshold S_n solvable iff n ≤ 4 (57 theorems in the extension file), and the known positive results (abelian, solvable, symmetric groups). The 2 remaining axioms (Kronecker-Weber, Shafarevich) are blocked on Mathlib infrastructure gaps. The 2 sorries are the open conjecture itself and symmetric group realizability (needs Hilbert irreducibility).
conclusion.implications:
The IGP has profound implications:

1. **ABSOLUTE GALOIS GROUP**: A positive answer would mean the absolute Galois group Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) surjects onto every finite group — revealing its structure.

2. **GALOIS REPRESENTATIONS**: The IGP is connected to the theory of Galois representations, central to the Langlands program and the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem.

3. **ARITHMETIC GEOMETRY**: Via Grothendieck's programme, the IGP connects to the study of algebraic curves and their fundamental groups.

4. **ALGORITHM DESIGN**: Positive answers might come with explicit polynomial constructions, useful for cryptography and computation.

5. **DIFFERENTIAL GALOIS THEORY**: The analogous question for differential equations (Kovacic's problem) has been solved, suggesting approaches for the classical case.
